canBeEqualForTwoCaptures: Yes. The value has millisecond resolution and comes from a wall clock: two captures within one

captures of one assignment are separated by its writes (R4: .255Z and .428Z); nothing forbids equality.

recency. The route description says so.

r4: The card was generated from the post-assignment snapshot (unit at revision 2) and the record is at

decision: The words are the ambiguous part: a field called snapshotState in the answer to a request that carries a
snapshot scope can be read as 'the state of the scope I sent'. The contract never says that and the
three card reads agree with each other, so no behaviour changes.
The contract entries gain descriptions that are published with the schema: the scope names the site and
is checked, it neither selects nor qualifies rows; targetRevision belongs to the card;
currentTargetRevision is the record now; snapshotState compares those two and not the scope passed.
whatAClientCannotLearnFromARow: Whether the card was generated from the scope it passed: a row does not carry the card's own manifest
id. An additive field could state it; it is not added here.
